notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Borough school districts are part of the borough government in Alaska, so school spending is included (it is left out of the services and overhead shares).
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($2,281,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money is not scored: no mayor and assembly candidates of Lake and Peninsula Borough reported contributions to the Alaska Public Offices Commission since 2023. Some municipalities run their own campaign disclosure instead.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-14. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Alaska yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
